CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zuexact computes sums of doubles exactly and rounds once, so results are the correctly rounded true value on every platform and in every element order. It vendors Radford Neal’s xsum (MIT) and exposes it as R functions with the xsum_ prefix (xsum() itself is the main entry point) and as a registered C table for other packages. Zero hard runtime dependencies. It never does arbitrary precision, decimals, or compensated-but-inexact summation (Kahan and friends live in PreciseSums).

.agents/design.md is the specification and .agents/roadmap.md the plan to 0.1.0. They outrank this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides.

Current state

0.1.0 is on CRAN, published 2026-10-22; main is at 0.1.0.9000 (verified 2026-11-11). Exported: xsum(), xsum_mean(), xsum_weighted_mean(), xsum_cumsum(), xsum_dot(), xsum_sqnorm(), xsum_norm(), the accumulator values (xsum_acc(), xsum_add(), xsum_merge(), xsum_negate(), xsum_value(), xsum_mean_value()), xsum_rowsums(), xsum_colsums(), xsum_by() and zuexact_info(), plus the registered C table zuexact_api_v1 (inst/include/zuexact.h). Results are proven against exact rationals, PreciseSums::fsum(), the test262 vectors and ill-conditioned inputs, and must be bit-identical on every CI leg.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is v0.1.1 (#25). The 0.1.0 parent was #2 and its submission issue #12. No sibling depends on zuexact yet; daffiz and qio are the candidate consumers of the C table, which is why it is append-only (see Invariants).

Merges are merge commits. The repository ruleset on main requires pull requests and allows only the merge method; squash is refused.

Commands

Run from the package root. The everyday devtools loop is in .claude/shared/r-package.md; these are the package’s own.

tools/vendor/verify                  # vendored tree == upstream + patches
tools/xsum-check/run [iters [seed]]  # upstream checker and fuzzer
tools/run-benchmarks                 # small/large threshold (C, no R)
R CMD INSTALL .                      # benchmarks need an installed build
Rscript -e 'library(zuexact); source("tools/bench/functions.R")'
Rscript -e 'library(zuexact); source("tools/bench/matrix.R")'
tools/write-bits                     # rewrite the bits fixture (rarely)
ZUEXACT_SLOW_TESTS=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'  # wider oracle sweeps

The tools/ scripts are for vendoring changes and need curl and a C compiler.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • One pass, then a rescan only when the result is not finite (src/zxe_sum.c). The rescan must skip exactly what na.rm = TRUE removed, including a complex element dropped because its other part is NaN; it once did not, and xsum(c(NA, Inf), na.rm = TRUE) gave NA.
  • An xsum_acc is 568 raw bytes: an 8-byte header (magic ZXAC, layout version, byte order, special-value flags) and one xsum small accumulator (src/zxe_accval.c). R’s NA/NaN distinction lives in the header flags, because xsum keeps a single NaN by payload. Changing the layout means bumping the version byte; the C table (Stage 6) operates on the same bytes. Locals are zeroed before use so no uninitialised padding is serialised.
  • Benchmark an installed package, never load_all(), which compiles at -O0: it doubled xsum_dot()’s time when first measured.
  • R_FINITE() is a function call in package code (R_finite()); hot loops use C99 isfinite().
  • tests/testthat/fixtures/bits.txt is the cross-platform contract. A changed line is a portability bug, never a reason to rerun tools/write-bits; that tool is for adding cases.
  • Cross-platform inputs never come from decimal literals that are not exact. R’s own parser differs between builds: on macOS ARM64 (no long double) 1e308 reads as 0x1.1ccf385ebc8a3p+1023, three ulps from the correctly rounded …8a0 that Linux gives. That broke the bits test once (2026-10-13). Build such inputs from bit patterns (from_hex()).
  • ALTREP() decides how a vector is read. ALTREP vectors go through *_GET_REGION into a stack block; REAL_RO() on one would materialise it.
  • One rounding. Every function rounds the exact value once, except where its documentation states the count (xsum_norm() two, xsum_weighted_mean() three). Never add an intermediate double between accumulation and the final round.
  • zuexact.so exports R_init_zuexact only ($(C_VISIBILITY) in src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win), and links no stdio, abort, exit or RNG symbol. tests/testthat/test-abi.R audits both on Linux and macOS.
  • The C table is append-only (inst/include/zuexact.h). Add members at the end and let struct_size tell consumers; any other change is a new name, zuexact_api_v2. tools/zuexacttest is the consumer that proves it (consumer.yaml).
  • Never trust a software fma(). mingw-w64’s (Windows, Rtools) gave wrong error terms. src/zxe_twoprod.h uses fma() only under FP_FAST_FMA and Dekker’s splitting otherwise; define ZXE_NO_FMA to test the Dekker branch on a machine with hardware FMA.
  • TwoProduct must not be contracted (design §9, §13). The files that include zxe_twoprod.h (zxe_dot.c, zxe_api.c) carry #pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF and keep p = x*y and e = fma(x, y, -p) in separate statements. -ffp-contract=off cannot be used: R CMD check reports -f flags as non-portable.
  • Symbol prefixes. Internal C symbols are prefixed zxe_; the public C table and header use zuexact_.
  • Condition classes are named zuexact_<kind>, for example zuexact_invalid_argument, not the <pkg>_<kind>_error pattern of .claude/shared/r-package.md. Tests assert on these classes.
  • Prose is en-GB, in roxygen and Markdown alike.

Testing

  • Oracles before hand-written cases (design §11): exact rationals with gmp (helper-oracle.R), PreciseSums::fsum(), the Math.sumPrecise test262 vectors (fixtures/sumprecise/, as bit patterns), and the Ogita–Rump–Oishi ill-conditioned generators (helper-illcond.R). ZUEXACT_SLOW_TESTS=true widens every sweep and ZUEXACT_SKIP_HEAVY=true (set by the gctorture leg) shrinks it to two inputs (family rule R7, sweep_reps() in helper-illcond.R).
  • Keep the CRAN suite under 15 s. It ran in 6.6 s on 2026-10-13 (macOS ARM64, CRAN settings).
  • Helpers live in tests/testthat/helper-*.R: helper-abi.R reads the shared object’s exported and undefined symbols with nm; helper-vendor.R defines selftest(), which sums through both xsum accumulators directly; helper-data.R makes random matrices spread over 80 binades; helper-oracle.R holds the exact rational oracle (exact_sum(), exact_dot()), whose round_bigq() exists because gmp’s as.double() truncates instead of rounding.
  • Done includes the nold leg (R without long doubles) being green: it is the leg this package exists for.

Continuous integration

Workflows call pedrobtz/r-actions: R-CMD-check.yaml (r-cmd-check.yml@v1, nold: true), coverage.yaml (coverage.yml, pinned to a commit because it holds a write token; badge on gh-pages because main takes no direct pushes), native-checks.yaml (sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers, CRAN special checks), vendor.yaml, vendor-upstream.yaml (weekly), and xsum-check.yaml (upstream’s checker, fuzzer and the threshold benchmark on three OSes, outside R), consumer.yaml (the C table from tools/zuexacttest) and fuzz.yaml (libFuzzer on tools/fuzz/fuzz_xsum.c: two minutes on pull requests, 30 minutes weekly on Sundays). pkgdown.yaml deploys with force: false so it does not overwrite the badge commit.

Deviation from .claude/shared/ci.md: R-CMD-check.yaml and native-checks.yaml choose the profile themselves rather than passing profile: auto. They run quick on pull requests and full on every push to main, so a merge does start the full set here. The full-ci label runs the full profile on a pull request.

Vendored native code

xsum by Radford M. Neal, MIT, pinned at tag stable-version-3, commit b766b3e (2024-11-13), in src/vendor/xsum/. tools/vendor/manifest.tsv pins it; tools/vendor/checksums.sha256 records the installed files; the one local patch is tools/patches/xsum/0001-no-stdio-exact-only.patch. Never edit src/vendor/ by hand: change the patch and run tools/vendor/fetch. The vendor.yaml workflow rejects a pull request that changes the tree without the manifest and checksums, and vendor-upstream.yaml opens an issue weekly when upstream tags a newer stable version.
